queries.hook: I can't focus, my mind is restless. Inside, my mind won't settle, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: The mind can be trained slowly, by practice and letting go; each time it wanders, it can be gently brought back.
queries.act: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.

hook.speaker: Bhasa
hook.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
hook.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
hook.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
hook.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
hook.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

alternates.speaker: Nidagha
alternates.sanskrit: पदं करोत्यलङ्घ्येऽपि तृप्ता विफलमीहते । चिरं तिष्ठति नैकत्र तृष्णा चपलमर्कटी ॥
alternates.line: Craving is a restless monkey: never in one place, never satisfied, reaching even where it cannot go.
alternates.translation: It sets foot even where no one can go; even when satisfied it strives in vain; it never stays long in one place: craving is a restless monkey.
alternates.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
alternates.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
alternates.line: This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.
alternates.translation: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
alternates.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.for_you: Your mind races between what is done, what is happening, and what must come next. You want others to like you, yet the list of things to do never ends. Rest is possible now, even while the tasks remain.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: After the story of two grieving brothers, Vasishtha tells Rama how worry feeds itself.
verse.sanskrit: चिन्तनेनैधते चिन्ता त्विन्धनेनेव पावकः । नश्यत्यचिन्ततेनैव विनेन्धनमिवानलः ॥
verse.line: Worry grows when you feed it thought, like fire with fuel. Starve it, and it dies down.
verse.translation: Worry grows by thinking, as fire grows with fuel; and it dies by not being thought, as fire dies without fuel.
verse.why: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

prasang.title: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die
prasang.summary: Two brothers live with their parents by the Ganga. When their father and mother die, the elder, Punya, performs the rites calmly while the younger, Pavana, wanders the forest weeping. Punya gently helps him see that the bonds of 'mine' and 'not mine' are made in the mind. Vasishtha draws the lesson: worry grows when fed, and a full mind finds the world full.
prasang.story_hook: When their parents died, one brother quietly lit the funeral fires and the other ran weeping into the forest.
prasang.lesson: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

verse.for_you: You are caught in a loop where every thought about what others think of you adds fuel to the worry. You do not have to keep feeding it. You can let it starve.
verse.try_today: Notice when the mind reaches for a thought about others. Let the thought drop without fuel.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
worry is shown to live on the attention it is fed

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: You keep turning the worry that others will not like you into proof that you are not enough. That self-contempt is eating the ground you stand on. The good that is trying to grow in you is being choked by it. Let that go.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you do not look down on yourself.

why: Think of strength, not of weakness.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From the section on wealth: on keeping your dignity before the rich.
verse.sanskrit: यद्धात्रा निजभालपट्टलिखितं स्तोकं महद्वा धनं तत् प्राप्नोति मरुस्थलेऽपि नितरां मेरौ ततो नाधिकम् । तद्धीरो भव वित्तवत्सु कृपणां वृत्तिं वृथा मा कृथाः कूपे पश्य पयोनिधावपि घटो गृह्णाति तुल्यं जलम् ॥
verse.line: A pot draws the same water from a well or the ocean. Keep your dignity before the rich.
verse.translation: Whatever wealth, small or great, the Creator has written on your forehead, you will get it even in a desert, and no more even on Mount Meru. So be steady; do not play the beggar before the rich for nothing. Look: a pot draws the same water from a well as from the ocean.
verse.why: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.
verse.misuse: Not a reason to stop working or asking for fair pay; a reason not to grovel.

matched.label: I keep comparing myself to others

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

verse.for_you: You are caught in a loop, worrying about whether others like you. A pot draws the same water from a well or the ocean. Keep your own dignity steady today.
verse.try_today: Notice when you are begging for approval, and stand still instead.
verse.scene_line: You stand before the well of the day, drawing the same water as the ocean.

why: No need to demean oneself before the rich

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: How a householder becomes a 'world' for others.
verse.sanskrit: यन्मनुष्यान्वासयते यदेभ्योऽशनं ददाति तेन मनुष्याणामथ यत्पशुभ्यस्तृणोदकं विन्दति तेन पशूनां यदस्य गृहेषु श्वापदा वयाꣳस्या पिपीलिकाभ्य उपजीवन्ति तेन तेषां लोको
verse.line: Feed people, find water for animals; when even ants live off your home, you become a world for them.
verse.translation: By housing people and giving them food, he becomes a world for people. By finding grass and water for animals, he becomes a world for animals. When beasts, birds and even ants live off his house, he becomes a world for them.

matched.label: I want to feel more grateful

verse.for_you: You are trying to make sure others like you, and your mind keeps turning it over. You are already a world for the ones who rest in your care.
verse.try_today: Notice one small way your home feeds or shelters something today.
verse.scene_line: The people and animals in your house live off your care, and you are a world for them.

why: a household is seen as something many lives rest on

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.for_you: You are tired from replaying the past and scripting the future for others. The mind is exhausted from wandering. It can rest. Whatever comes, comes. Take what arrives without looking for it.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today that arrives unplanned, and take it.
verse.scene_line: Beside the mind that wanders, your mind rests, taking what comes.

story.title: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps
story.story_hook: The poet of the Ramcharitmanas began life as an unwanted child begging for scraps in the lanes.
story.summary: Across his later works Tulsidas tells his own story: left by his parents at birth, he wandered door to door for scraps, no job, no trade, no skill, ignored by everyone. Good people told him not to worry; Hanuman raised him like a child; Ram's name, he says, turned a thorny babul into a mango tree. Even when he went astray, he was taken back.
story.lesson: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
story.hook_title: Tulsidas began life as an unwanted child begging for scraps
story.teaser: Tulsidas began life as an unwanted child begging for scraps
story.for_you: The mind keeps circling the need to be liked. You do not have to earn the room you are already in.
